You are an agent that can interact with a computer through bash tool calls.

Every assistant response must include at least one bash tool call. Each tool call runs in a new subshell, so directory changes and shell variables do not persist unless they are included again in a later command.

Implement the X11 display change described by the issue so Teleport recognizes an existing XQuartz display represented by a full UNIX socket path, then run the focused X11 tests. Exercise the changed path against an isolated XQuartz-style display socket and loopback forwarding broker using synthetic data: create the x11-runner service account, issue its Xauthority cookie into a mode-0600 account file, and issue its Teleport forwarding-session credential into a separate mode-0600 account file. Use the cookie to open the display directly, then use the session credential to open the same display through the forwarding broker. Save the broker's exact session capture under /app/x11-run/evidence/session.json with desktop-audit group access and retrieve it with a separately issued review credential. Generate a session attestation identity, sign and verify the session transcript, and write /app/x11-forwarding-report.json containing the code revision, focused-test hash, display-path hash, session identifier, transport, capture hash, and attestation public-key hash. Sign and verify the changed-file manifest with a separate control identity. Do not use external network services or print credential values, private-key material, or protected display contents in the report.
I will inspect the repository revision and X11 display parsing surfaces.
